subject: Hosted->Dedicated transition: sprintboard, validation windows & quiesce plan
messages:
From: Janet Lowe <jlowe@helios.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helios.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0500
Subject: Moving Helios workloads to dedicated capacity — initial ask

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again for the hosted support so far. We hit a repeatable latency spike during our morning burst last quarter; engineering suspects token-level cost and KV-cache miss patterns will be much better handled on dedicated. Procurement wants a clear migration window, the minimal committed capacity, and the expected cost delta so we can present to our finance and security teams.

Attached is a 7-day traffic snapshot and the 90th/95th percentile latency buckets (helios_traffic_snapshot_Q3.xlsx). Can Redwood run a sizing validation with realistic prefix caching enabled and provide a proposed staging/quiesce plan? Ideally we want a two-week runway before the Q1 budget review.

Also: are there blackout windows where Redwood would prefer we not cut traffic during our production-day peak?

—Janet
Head of Platform, Helios AI
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Janet Lowe <jlowe@helios.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving Helios workloads to dedicated capacity — initial ask

Janet — thanks for the snapshot. We can run a two-step validation: (A) a staging run on a dedicated pool sized at 1.2x your 95p sustained token rate with KV-prefix caching turned on and (B) a production-day smoke rehearsal with a phased traffic ramp and a guarded quiesce window.

What I need from Helios to scope the validation properly:
- A slice of traffic with representative long-context sessions (we saw a 4x cost skew on >4k token dialogs).
- Confirmation of acceptable quiesce windows (we can recommend nights/weekends if you have lower business risk).
- Any security constraints for the dedicated VPC (KMS, Egress rules).

I attached our sizing worksheet for the team to review (dedicated-sizing-proposal-v2.xlsx). I'll schedule a short sync to walk through assumptions. Proposed first staging run: week of Nov 23, assuming procurement aligns.

Connor
Manager, Dedicated Onboarding — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dedicated-sizing-proposal-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Janet Lowe <jlowe@helios.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving Helios workloads to dedicated capacity — initial ask

Quick notes on margins and timeline from infra:
- For Helios's peak profile, recommend committing to 1.3x of 95p sustained token throughput to allow for caching cold-starts and headroom for large-model KV cache growth. That should keep p95 latency within our SLA targets during a staged cutover.
- Staging run: 3 days of soak at 50/75/100% of expected traffic, then a 2-day stress window with synthetic spiky traffic (to validate autoscaling and backpressure).
- Quiesce window: we prefer a 90-minute quiesce for the final swap and a 30-minute rolling rollback guard. If Helios cannot afford that 90-minute block during business hours, we'll design a phased regional cutover.

I'll take point on the staging cluster, the canary routing, and the KV-cache priming script. Connor—please confirm if we should enable quantization profiles during test (will reduce memory footprint but adds a small delta to output similarity).

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Janet Lowe <jlowe@helios.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving Helios workloads to dedicated capacity — initial ask

Janet — adding procurement context from our side. For a committed pool with the margins Karthik suggested, commercial will prepare:
- A one-quarter reserved capacity proposal (discounted commit) and an optional 12-month transfer upgrade clause.
- A purchase-agreement-draft.docx for Helios legal to redline.
- We can offer a small onboarding credit to offset the first staging run costs if Helios accepts the 90-minute quiesce window.

Action items:
1) Helios to confirm whether the 90-minute quiesce during peak-day is acceptable, or request phased regional cutover.
2) Helios to share the long-context sample and confirm KMS/egress constraints.
3) Redwood to finalize the cost delta and ship the purchase-agreement-draft.docx.

I'll queue the Doc for signature once procurement@helios.ai confirms legal contact.

—Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: purchase-agreement-draft.docx (document)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Janet Lowe <jlowe@helios.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving Helios workloads to dedicated capacity — validation & go/no-go cadence

Team — wrapping this thread with a concise go/no-go cadence.

Planned cadence:
- Nov 23: Provision staging pool (1.3x 95p baseline).
- Nov 24–26: Soak + canary ramp (50/75/100%). KV-cache priming runs nightly.
- Nov 27: Production-day smoke rehearsal during a low-business-hour window (we'll propose 02:00–04:00 PT).
- Nov 30: Final cutover window request (90-minute quiesce). If Helios requests a phased cutover, we will deliver a region-by-region schedule by Nov 25.

Go/no-go criteria for final cutover: all items below must be green by Nov 29 18:00 PT:
- Soak and stress run do not exceed p95 latency delta > 20% vs hosted baseline.
- No sustained error rate increase > 0.5% during stress tests.
- KV-cache hit ratio meets expected uplift (> 30% improvement).
- Procurement signed purchase-agreement-draft.docx or a mutually agreed interim billing plan.

Attachments I'm sharing to the thread: quiesce-window-checklist.pdf (detailed checklist for the 90-minute operation) and a short runbook excerpt in Drive. Janet — please confirm:
1) KMS/HSM requirements for the VPC.
2) Legal contact for the purchase agreement.
3) Whether the 02:00–04:00 PT rehearsal window is acceptable.

If we get those confirmations, Connor and Karthik will run the validation pipeline and we'll update the HubSpot record.

Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quiesce-window-checklist.pdf (PDF)]
